verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              अहो धर्मिष्ठता तात वृत्रस्यामिततेजसः । यस्य विज्ञानमतुलं विष्णोर्भक्तिश्च तादृशी ॥१॥
verses.english: How great was the love of virtue possessed by Vritra of incomparable energy, whose knowledge was incomparable and whose devotion to Vishnu was so great.

verses.sanskrit: दुर्विज्ञेयं पदं तात विष्णोरमिततेजसः । कथं वा राजशार्दूल पदं तु ज्ञातवानसौ ॥२॥
verses.english: The position occupied by Vishnu of immeasurable energy is difficult, of being perceived. How, O foremost of kings, could Vritra comprehend it?

verses.sanskrit: भवता कथितं ह्येतच्छ्रद्दधे चाहमच्युतम् । भूयस्तु मे समुत्पन्ना बुद्धिरव्यक्तदर्शनात् ॥३॥
verses.english: You have described Vritra's acts. I too have heard you in full faith. Because, on account of my seeing that one point is unintelligible that my curiosity has been roused for asking you again.

verses.sanskrit: कथं विनिहतो वृत्रः शक्रेण पुरुषर्षभ । धार्मिको विष्णुभक्तश्च तत्त्वज्ञश्च पदान्वये ॥४॥
verses.english: How, indeed, was Vritra, who was virtuous, devoted to Vishnu, gifted with knowledge of truth derivable from a just comprehension of the Upanishads and Vedanta, defeated by Indra, O foremost of men.

verses.sanskrit: एतन्मे संशयं ब्रूहि पृच्छते भरतर्षभ । वृत्रस्तु राजशार्दूल यथा शक्रेण निर्जितः ॥५॥
verses.english: O king of the Bharatas, remove this my doubt! Indeed, tell me, O foremost of kings, how Vritra was defeated by Shakra.

verses.sanskrit: यथा चैवाभवद्युद्धं तच्चाचक्ष्व पितामह । विस्तरेण महाबाहो परं कौतूहलं हि मे ॥६॥
verses.english: O grandfather, O you of mighty arms, tell me fully how the battle took place. Great is my curiosity to hear it.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              रथेनेन्द्रः प्रयातो वै सार्धं देवगणैः पुरा । ददर्शाथाग्रतो वृत्रं धिष्ठितं पर्वतोपमम् ॥७॥
verses.english: Bhishma said-In days of yore, Indra, accompanied by the celestial army, proceeded on his car, and saw the Asura Vritra stationed before him like a mountain.

verses.sanskrit: योजनानां शतान्यूर्ध्वं पञ्चोच्छ्रितमरिंदम् । शतानि विस्तरेणाथ त्रीण्येवाभ्यधिकानि वै ॥८॥
verses.english: He was full five hundred Yojanas in height, 0 chastiser of enemies and three hundred Yojanas in circumference.

verses.sanskrit: तत्प्रेक्ष्य तादृशं रूपं त्रैलोक्येनापि दुर्जयम् । वृत्रस्य देवाः संत्रस्ता न शान्तिमुपलेभिरे ॥९॥
verses.english: Seeing that form of Vritra, which was incapable of being defeated by the three worlds united together, the celestials became stricken with fear and full of anxiety.

verses.sanskrit: शक्रस्य तु तदा राजन्नूरुस्तम्भो व्यजायत । भयाद्वृत्रस्य सहसा दृष्ट्वा तद्रूपमुत्तमम् ॥१०॥
verses.english: Indeed, suddenly beholding that huge form of his enemy, O king, Indra was paralysed in the lower extremities.

verses.sanskrit: ततो नादः समभवद्वादित्राणां च निःस्वनः । देवासुराणां सर्वेषां तस्मिन्युद्धे ह्युपस्थिते ॥११॥
verses.english: Then, on the eve of that great battle between the gods and the demons, there arose loud peals from both sides, and drums and other musical instruments were beaten and blown.

verses.sanskrit: अथ वृत्रस्य कौरव्य दृष्ट्वा शक्रमवस्थितम् । न सम्भ्रमो न भीः काचिदास्था वा समजायत ॥१२॥
verses.english: Seeing Indra stationed before him, you of Kuru's race, Vritra felt neither awe nor fear, nor was he disposed to collect all his energies for the battle.

verses.sanskrit: ततः समभवद्युद्धं त्रैलोक्यस्य भयंकरम् । शक्रस्य च सुरेन्द्रस्य वृत्रस्य च महात्मनः ॥१३॥
verses.english: Then the battle took place filling the three worlds with fear, between Indra the king of the gods and Vritra of great energy.

verses.sanskrit: असिभिः पट्टिशैः शूलैः शक्ति-तोमर-मुद्गरैः । शिलाभिर्विविधाभिश्च कार्मुकैश्च महास्वनैः ॥१४॥
verses.english: The entire sky was covered by the warriors of both sides with swords, axes, lances, darts, spears and heavy clubs and rocks of various sizes and bows of loud sound and various sorts of celestial weapons and fires and burning brands.

verses.sanskrit: शस्त्रैश्च विविधैर्दिव्यैः पावकोल्काभिरेव च । देवासुरैस्ततः सैन्यैः सर्वमासीत्समाकुलम् ॥१५॥
पितामहपुरोगाश्च सर्वे देवगणास्तथा । ऋषयश्च महाभागास्तद्युद्धं द्रष्टुमागमन् ॥१६॥
verses.english: All the deities led by the Grand-father, and all the highly-blessed Rishis, came to see the battle, on their best of cars; and the Siddhas, also, O foremost of Bharata's family, and the Gandharvas, with the Apsaras, on their own beautiful and foremost of cars, came there.

verses.sanskrit: विमानाग्र्यैर्महाराज सिद्धाश्च भरतर्षभ । गन्धर्वाश्च विमानाग्र्यैरप्सरोभिः समागमन् ॥१७॥
ततोऽन्तरिक्षमावृत्य वृत्रो धर्मभृतां वरः । अश्वमवर्षेण देवेन्द्रं समाकिरदतिद्रुतम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: Then Vritra, that foremost of virtuous persons, speedily overwhelmed the sky and the king of gods with a thick shower of rocks.

verses.sanskrit: ततो देवगणाः क्रुद्धाः सर्वतः शरवृष्टिभिः । अश्मवर्षमपोहन्त वृत्रप्रेरितमाहवे ॥१९॥
verses.english: Thereat, filled with ire the celestials dispelled with their showers of arrows that thick down-pour of rocks showered by Vritra in battle.

verses.sanskrit: वृत्रस्तु कुरुशार्दूल महामायो महाबलः । मोहयामास देवेन्द्रं मायायुद्धेन सर्वशः ॥२०॥
verses.english: Then Vritra, O foremost of Kurus, endued with mighty strength and large powers of illusion, stupefied the king of illusion. was

verses.sanskrit: तस्य वृत्रार्दितस्याथ मोह आसीच्छतक्रतोः । रथन्तरेण तं तत्र वसिष्ठः समबोधयत् ॥२१॥
verses.english: When the god of hundred sacrifices, thus afflicted by Vritra, possessed by stupefaction, the sage Vashishtha restores him to his senses by chanting Samans.

verses.sanskrit: वसिष्ठ उवाच । देवश्रेष्ठोऽसि देवेन्द्र दैत्यासरुनिबर्हण । त्रैलोक्यबलसंयुक्तः कस्माच्छक्र विषीदसि ॥२२॥
verses.english: Vashishtha said You are the foremost of the gods, O chief of the gods, O destroyer of Daityas and Asuras! The strength of the three worlds lies in you! Why, then, O Shakra, do you languish so!

verses.sanskrit: एष ब्रह्मा च विष्णुश्च शिवश्चैव जगत्पतिः । सोमश्च भगवान्देवः सर्वे च परमर्षयः ॥२३॥
verses.english: See, there are Brahma and Vishnu, and Shiva, that lord of the universe, the illustrious and divine Soma, and all the great Rishis.

verses.sanskrit: माकार्षीः कश्मलं शक्र कश्चिदेवेतरो यथा । आर्यां युद्धे मतिं कृत्वा जहि शत्रून्सुराधिप ॥२४॥
verses.english: Do not, O Indra, yield to weakness, like an ordinary mortal! Firmly determined on battle, kill your enemies, O king of the gods.

verses.sanskrit: एष लोकगुरुस्त्र्यक्षः सर्वलोकनमस्कृतः । निरीक्षते त्वां भगवांस्त्यज मोहं सुराधिप ॥२५॥
verses.english: There, that lord of all the worlds, viz., the Three-eyed (Shiva), worshipped of all the worlds, is seeing you! Shake off this stupefaction, O king of the gods.

verses.sanskrit: एते ब्रह्मर्षयश्चैव बृहस्पतिपुरोगमाः । स्तवेन शक्र दिव्येन स्तुवन्ति त्वां जयाय वै ॥२६॥
verses.english: There, those twice-born Rishis, headed by Brihaspati, are lauding you for your victory, in celestial hymns.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              एवं सम्बोध्यमानस्य वसिष्ठेन महात्मना । अतीव वासवस्यासीद्बलमुत्तमतेजसः ॥२७॥
verses.english: Bhishma said-While the highly energetic Vasava was thus being restored to senses by the great Vashishtha, his strength became greatly increased.

verses.sanskrit: ततो बुद्धिमुपागम्य भगवान्पाकशासनः । योगेन महता युक्तस्तां मायां व्यपकर्षत ॥२८॥
verses.english: The illustrious punisher of Paka then, depending upon his intelligence, had recourse to high Yoga and with its help removed these illusions of Vritra.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽङ्गिरःसुतः श्रीमांस्ते चैव सुमहर्षयः । दृष्ट्वा वृत्रस्य विक्रान्तमुपागम्य महेश्वरम् ॥२९॥
verses.english: Then Brihaspati, the son of Angiras, and those greatest of Rishis endued with great prosperity, seeing the prowess of Vritra, went to Mahadeva, and moved by the desire of benefiting the three worlds, urged him to kill the great Asura.

verses.sanskrit: ऊचुर्वृत्रविनाशार्थं लोकानां हितकाम्यया । ततो भगवतस्तेजो ज्वरो भूत्वा जगत्पतेः ॥३०॥
समाविशत्तदा रौद्रो वृत्रं लोकपतिं तदा । विष्णुश्च भगवान्देवः सर्वलोकाभिपूजितः ॥३१॥
ऐन्द्रं समाविशद्वज्रं लोकसंरक्षणे रतः । ततो बृहस्पतिर्धीमानुपागम्य शतक्रतुम् । वसिष्ठश्च महातेजाः सर्वे च परमर्षयः ॥३२॥
ते समासाद्य वरदं वासवं लोकपूजितम् । ऊचुरेकाग्रमनसो जहि वृत्रमिति प्रभो ॥३३॥
महेश्वर उवाच । एष वृत्रो महाशक्र बलेन महता वृतः । विश्वात्मा सर्वगश्चैव बहुमायश्च विश्रुतः ॥३४॥
तदेनमसुरश्रेष्ठं त्रैलोक्येनापि दुर्जयम् । जहि त्वं योगमास्थाय माऽवमंस्थाः सुरेश्वर ॥३५॥
verses.english: This foremost of Asuras is, therefore incapable of being defeated by even the threeworlds in a body. Helped by Yoga, do you kill him, O king of the celestials. Do not neglect him.

verses.sanskrit: अनेन हि तपस्तप्तं बलार्थममराधिप । षष्टिं वर्षसहस्राणि ब्रह्मा चास्मै वरं ददौ ॥३६॥
verses.english: O king of the celestials, Vritra had practised, for full sixty thousand years, the severest penances for acquiring strength. Brahma gave him the boons he had prayed for, viz., the greatness that belongs to Yogins, large powers of illusion, enough of might, and superabundant energy.

verses.sanskrit: महत्त्वं योगिनां चैव महामायत्वमेव च । महाबलत्त्वं च तथा तेजश्चाग्र्यं सुरेश्वर ॥३७॥
एतत्त्वां मामकं तेजः समाविशति वासव । व्यग्रमेनं त्वमप्येनं वज्रेण जहि दानवम् ॥३८॥
verses.english: I give you my energy, O Vasava! The Danava has now lost his coolness. Do you, therefore, kill him now with your thunderbolt.

verses.sanskrit: शक्र उवाच । भगवंस्त्वत्प्रसादेन दितिजं सुदुरासदम् । वज्रेण निहनिष्यामि पश्यतस्ते सुरर्षभ ॥३९॥
verses.english: Shakra said Before your eyes, O foremost of gods, I shall, through your favour kill with my thunderbolt this invincible son Diti.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              आविश्यमाने दैत्ये तु ज्वरेणाथ महासुरे । देवतानामृषीणां च हर्षान्नादो महानभूत् ॥४०॥
verses.english: Bhishma said. When the great Asura or Daitya was possessed by that fever, the gods and the Rishis, filled with joy, sent up loud cheers.

verses.sanskrit: ततो दुन्दुभयश्चैव शङ्खाश्च सुमहास्वनाः । मुरजा डिण्डिमाश्चैव प्रावाद्यन्त सहस्रशः ॥४१॥
असुराणां तु सर्वेषां स्मृतिलोपो महानभूत् । मायानाशश्च बलवान्क्षणेन समपद्यत ॥४२॥
verses.english: Suddenly all the Asuras lost in a body their memory. At that moment their powers of illusion, also, disappeared.

verses.sanskrit: तथाविष्टमथो ज्ञात्वा ऋषयो देवतास्तथा । स्तुवन्तः शक्रमीशानं तथा प्राचोदयन्नपि ॥४३॥
verses.english: Knowing the enemy to be thus possessed, the Rishis and gods lauded both Shakra and Ishana, and began to urge the former.

verses.sanskrit: रथस्थस्य हि शक्रस्य युद्धकाले महात्मनः । ऋषिभिः स्तूयमानस्य रूपमासीत्सुदुर्दृशम् ॥४४॥
verses.english: The form that Indra assumed on the eve of the battle, while seated on his car and while his praises were being lauded by the Rishis, became such that none could look at it without dread.
